original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Profile the selected PR6030 primary verifier (research/p104-helper470-twin-rung-removal/verify.py, run twice by make frontier6030-verify) and remove its measured bottleneck, clifford_exact.Op.zero_state, by binding the already merged gate-table evaluator research/clifford-state-performance/fast_state.py to the byte-identical clifford_exact.py copy that PR6030's chain loads, without editing any frozen file.
scope_change_reason: Refined from the generic card to one fixture (the selected replay's primary stage) and one bottleneck. The table method is not new: it is Charles Bethin's fast_state.py (PR662 lineage), reused unchanged; the new parts are the source-bound binding to this consumer, an exhaustive differential over its real workload, and same-fixture timings.
bottleneck_link: The primary verifier is the longest stage of the selected replay and runs twice (normal and -O), each under a 600 s stage timeout; the maintainer audit recorded 228 s and 461 s. Halving it shortens every review of P104 successors that reuse PR5827's chain.
stop_rule: Stop after one bottleneck: same-fixture before/after timings, an exhaustive differential over every zero_state call of the real run, and invalidation controls. Do not optimize the next hotspot or edit scripts/audit_p1046030.py (maintainer decision).
evidence: cProfile: Op.zero_state is 202 of 280 profiled seconds. Same fixture, serial fresh processes on Apple M5 / CPython 3.12.14: normal stage 107.0-120.4 s -> 47.3-47.6 s (2.39x of medians), -O stage 62.2-62.9 s -> 41.7-42.0 s (1.50x). Differential: all 32,766 calls equal; the unchanged verifier's own RESULT.json byte check passes in every mode. test_equivalence: 1,714 random states, 280 lowered children, 48 frames, 3 mutants rejected, changed compiler bytes and all 14 changed pins refused. Raw samples in BENCHMARK.json.
